ed1-P2.text: edition 1: Pioneering (speculative): per-certificate reflection expressible, wholesale reflection inexpressible, as a language-level answer to Loeb's obstacle.

ed1-T0.text: edition 1: Byte-identical receipts across the reference, Python, C99 and Rust show integrity on this host; standing is non-factive and no truth predicate exists in the language.

ed1-T1.text: edition 1: Per-certificate explicit reflection is expressible and wholesale reflection is not (Artemov's Logic of Proofs against Loeb's theorem).

ed1-T2.text: edition 1: A claim by computation carries no external bits (data processing inequality); GROUNDED requires a ledger line the program cannot write.

ed1-T3.text: edition 1: A certificate whose counted cost is at most half its clause's reads cheap; it is GROUNDED only with a ratified determinacy theorem (Blum 1988 little-oh, bounded by Urdr L28).

ed1-T4.text: edition 1: Claims in gfp minus lfp of the support operator are exactly the circularly supported ones; when lfp equals gfp every self-consistent trust assignment gives the same standing.

ed1-T5.text: edition 1: Fixed and floating point are deterministic by construction under the declared envelope; four-way byte identity here; Orlog's generated C has no FMA under contraction-allowing flags.

ed1-T6.text: edition 1: The door repairs only bytes the grammar reads identically, preserves literal contents, refuses the rest, and is a retraction.

ed1-T7.text: edition 1: Fixed-point position Verlet is exactly reversible and pairwise impulses conserve momentum exactly; both are runtime oracles.

ed1-T8.text: edition 1: Prose is a lossless spelling of a typed law: three spellings give one law-seal.

ed1-T9.text: edition 1: A chaotic map magnifies a one-ulp difference to the whole value; with traces, divergence is localized at the first differing operation.
